passage:
"Mummy, listen to this," Hemant said, holding up his laptop. "A guy called Omkar wrote under my article. Very polite. He says my chart has the wrong year for the rainfall data."
"Wrong? You checked it three times."
"I know. That's why my face is hot." He scrolled. "But he's right. I typed 2019 instead of 2018."
"So write back and say he's mistaken."
"Mummy, no. He isn't mistaken. He took the time to check my work." Hemant typed: "Thank you, Omkar, you're right. Fixed, and I've added a correction note at the top 🙏"
"Now everybody will see you made an error."
"Better they see me fix it than see me argue." He pressed publish and let out a breath.

qa.q: What error did Omkar point out in Hemant's article?
qa.a: Omkar said the chart had the wrong year, 2019 instead of 2018.

qa.q: Why did Hemant thank Omkar even though his face felt hot?
qa.a: The mistake stung, but Hemant saw that Omkar was polite, was right, and had taken the time to check the work.

qa.q: What made Hemant's response a sensible way to handle the mistake?
qa.a: He thanked the critic, fixed the chart and added a visible correction note. Owning the error openly is more credible than arguing.

qa.q: How might Mummy see Hemant's decision to publish a correction?
qa.a: She seems to worry that everyone will see the error, so she probably sees it as embarrassing. She may see it differently once she notices he stays calm.

grounding: A stranger politely points out a real error; it stings, but Hemant thanks them, fixes it and publishes a correction.

passage:
Pema: Hi Jatin, I read your article on Himalayan birds, loved it 🙂
Pema: Small thing: the photo labelled "blood pheasant" is actually a satyr tragopan. Easy to mix up in bad light.
Jatin: Oh.
Jatin: I checked it twice 😳
Jatin: Give me a minute
Jatin: ...you're right. The red head and the spots. Ugh.
Pema: It happens to everyone. The rest of the piece is lovely.
Jatin: Honestly my first reaction was to get defensive. Thank you for telling me so kindly.
Jatin: Fixing it now and adding a correction note at the bottom with your name, if that's ok?
Pema: Sure! And thank you for fixing it quickly
Jatin: Would you ever want to write a guest piece? You clearly know more than me
Pema: Haha maybe! Let's talk

qa.q: What bird did Jatin mistake the satyr tragopan for?
How can you tell Jatin felt stung at first?
qa.a: Jatin's short "Oh." and "I checked it twice" show embarrassment and defensiveness before looking again.

qa.q: Which of Jatin's choices built the most credibility?
qa.a: Thanking Pema, fixing the error and adding a public correction note, instead of arguing.

qa.q: How does Pema see Jatin's response?
qa.a: Pema seems pleased and warm, thanking Jatin for fixing it quickly and open to writing a guest piece.

grounding: The chat shows someone whose work gets a polite correction from a stranger, feeling stung, then thanking them, fixing it and publishing a correction.

passage:
Every Friday Yamini posted the Sirsi town news on the local community page: rainfall, market prices, school results, who needed blood donors. Four thousand people followed it.

On Saturday morning, Pallavi-teacher, retired from the girls' school, stopped Yamini outside the vegetable shop. "Your post said the dam gates open Monday. The notice at the taluk office says Wednesday. Farmers downstream might move their cattle too early."

Yamini's cheeks went hot. She had rushed that post at midnight.

"Are you sure?" slipped out, sharper than she meant.

Pallavi-teacher just held out her phone with a photo of the notice.

Yamini looked, then breathed out. "You're right. Thank you, really."

She posted the correction before she even reached home: "Correction: dam gates open WEDNESDAY, not Monday. My mistake. Thanks to a reader for pointing it out." By evening, more people had shared the correction than the original.

qa.q: According to the taluk office notice, when would the dam gates open?
What was Yamini feeling when Pallavi-teacher pointed out the error?
qa.a: Yamini felt embarrassed and a bit defensive, her cheeks going hot and "Are you sure?" slipping out sharply.

qa.q: What did Yamini get right after checking the notice?
qa.a: She thanked Pallavi-teacher and posted a clear correction right away, owning the mistake openly.

qa.q: How might Pallavi-teacher see Yamini's quick correction?
qa.a: Pallavi-teacher may feel respected and reassured that the farmers would get the right date, and trust the page more.

grounding: The passage shows someone whose public work contains a genuine error, politely pointed out; it stings, but she thanks the critic, fixes it and publishes a correction.
